summary: Cape Race's 1856 cast-iron tower, moved to the Cape North (Money Point) light in 1908-1911 and retired in 1980, now stands at Ottawa's science museum.

lens.where: lantern room, Canada Science and Technology Museum, Ottawa

structures.note: Built at Cape Race, Newfoundland; at Money Point, Cape North, 1908/1911 to 1980; now on the museum grounds in Ottawa.

staffing.note: Money Point light (NSLPS 'Cape North III'), not the Ottawa tower.

access.note: Tower and grounds at the museum in Ottawa; LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower open in season.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard for the Money Point station to 1980; Canada Science and Technology Museum for the tower since 1980.

events.note: Cast-iron tower at Cape Race, Newfoundland (Ingenium; LighthouseFriends).
Rotating mechanism installed in the Cape Race tower (LighthouseFriends).
Earlier wooden tower at Money Point (NSLPS: began 1875, lit 1876). This is the station's first light, before the Cape Race tower came.
Revolving red and white catoptric light at the Money Point wooden tower (NSLPS).
3-inch diaphone in the new fog-alarm building at North cape (Department report, fiscal 1908); NSLPS dates the air diaphone to 1908.
Dismantled and moved to Money Point. Ingenium gives 1908; Rowlett 1907; LighthouseFriends 1909; the Department's 1910 report describes it being erected.
Iron tower from Cape Race replaced the 1876 wooden tower at Money Point; first shown 1911 (LighthouseFriends; NSLPS).
A 3rd order single flashing light placed at Cape North (Department report, fiscal 1911).
Flashing white light at the Money Point iron tower (NSLPS).
Dismantled at Money Point and moved to the Ottawa museum (LighthouseFriends; Ingenium).
Went dark in early October 1980, after a temporary light was set up (LighthouseFriends); inactive since 1980 (Rowlett).
Money Point light replaced by a skeleton tower, 'Lighthouse IV' (NSLPS).
Earthquake spilled part of the mercury that floated the lens; staff cleaned it up and a contractor decontaminated the tower (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: Rowlett gives the iron tower as 14 m (46 ft); NSLPS gives 47 ft for the Money Point tower of 1911. The Wikidata figure of 29.0 m matches neither.

The name 'Cape North' refers to the light station at Money Point, Victoria County, Nova Scotia (1911 to 1980). The Ottawa tower is a museum object that the station once used. The editor must decide whether this record describes the tower or the station, and whether the station needs its own record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The tower was built at Cape Race in 1856 (Ingenium, LighthouseFriends, Rowlett). The move to Cape North is dated 1907 (Rowlett), 1908 (Ingenium), 1909 (LighthouseFriends) and 1911 (NSLPS, service start). The Department's 1910 report says the old Cape Race tower was still being erected at the site that year, so the move is treated as 1908 to 1911.

notes_for_editor: Identity: the record's id and location describe the Ottawa tower, but the station it names is the Cape North light at Money Point, Nova Scotia (1875-76 wooden tower; 1911-1980 iron tower from Cape Race; 1980 square wooden tower; 2009 skeleton tower, NSLPS). The story now names the Money Point station first and treats the Ottawa tower as the structure that served it. The editor should decide whether to split the record. Fiscal years: the 1900-1906 Marine reports cover the year ended 30 June; from 1908 the reports cover the twelve months ended 31 March. The story uses those labels, and the 1905 collision (12 September 1905) is in the 1905 report because it covers work since 30 June. 1908 'North cape' entry: printed p. 67 (scan 76), in the Nova Scotia section after Westville, N.S.; PEI's section begins later (p. 70), so this is Cape North, Nova Scotia, not PEI's North Cape. Checked in the text, not on the page image. 1909 'Cape Xorth' double dwelling: an OCR heading in the Nova Scotia list next to Margaree (scan 63, printed 56); checked in the text, not on the page image. 1910 row: checked on the page image (PDF page 82, printed p. 81, scan 81). The 'St. George, cape North, cape' station label spans two rows; 'Lighthouse tower repairs' is on the St. George row and 'Erection of a new reinforced steel concrete tower' is on the North, cape row, so the parenthetical about the Cape Race tower belongs to Cape North. 1905 collision: the vessel heading reads 'Ohristian-Knudsen-Thrift' in the OCR (scan 197); the story does not name the vessel and the page image was not checked. Keepers: none matched. The Cape North (Money Point) names in the 1902, 1908 and 1911 keeper tables (Mauger, McLeod, McKay) are not linked; the page images for fiscal 1902 (scan 244), 1908 (scan 189) and 1911 (scans 242, 256) should be read before any roster line is added. Rowlett and LighthouseFriends disagree on public access: LighthouseFriends says the tower is open in season, Rowlett says the tower is closed. The story states both. NSLPS prints the 1883 optic as 'catatropic lens' (sic); the story says 'revolving red and white light'. Ingenium's object height (19.52 m) is not used: the page says its dimensions are storage sizes. The 1876 Money Point wooden tower is a different structure and is recorded only as an event. Copyright: LighthouseFriends and NSLPS text is paraphrased; quotations are short. Wikipedia used as a lead only.
